units.why: Transparency "develops and maintains trust and credibility for all stakeholders" gives a reason for disclosure; P24 is nearest since there is no fairness (P95) or skill claim.

units.passage: Students communicate the ways they engage with and use AI tools in support of their learning process and any products they create.
units.why: Students 'communicate the ways they engage with and use AI tools in support of their learning process and any products they create' describes student transparency; disclosure, P24.

units.passage: It is your decision (except where it is a requirement for a course or job) to disclose use of AI.

units.passage: If required, cite your use of AI. Examples of Formal Citation Standards for AI .
units.why: "If required, cite your use of AI" is a conditional citation duty, P24.

units.passage: Acknowledge when and how you used them
units.why: "Acknowledge when and how you used them" requires disclosure of AI use, P24.

units.passage: When in doubt, err on the side of acknowledgment.
units.why: 'When in doubt, err on the side of acknowledgment' tells students to disclose when unsure; P24.

units.passage: Properly cite AI-generated content in academic work.
units.why: 'Properly cite AI-generated content in academic work'; P24.

units.passage: However, the use of such tools must be documented and clearly cited in all submitted work
units.why: "the use of such tools must be documented and clearly cited in all submitted work" requires disclosure with each submission (P24).

units.passage: Students must clearly identify writing, text, or media generated by AI and show how AI tools were used in the process of creating a final product
units.why: Students 'must clearly identify writing, text, or media generated by AI and show how AI tools were used in the process of creating a final product' requires disclosure of AI-generated content with the submission, plus a description of process (P24).

units.passage: When allowed, students must clearly identify writing, text, or media generated by AI and show how AI tools were used in the process of creating a final product.
units.why: "When allowed, students must clearly identify writing, text, or media generated by AI" requires disclosure when use is allowed (P24).

units.passage: When students are allowed to use generative AI tools, they may be required to cite the tools that are used and/or provide specific information about their use.
units.why: "they may be required to cite the tools that are used and/or provide specific information about their use" says instructors may require citation and details (P24).

units.passage: Rather than all out prohibiting AI usage, one approach educators are using to address issues of information origin is to require students who use AI to reflect on and cite their use of AI tools
units.why: The page says 'one approach educators are using' is 'to require students who use AI to reflect on and cite their use of AI tools'. This offers requiring disclosure as an option to instructors who do not prohibit AI, so it is P24 with modality may.

units.passage: In accordance with university policies around academic integrity in the Student Code of Conduct, we will be transparent in our use of AI in the completion of any classroom tasks. And, although there are questions around how and whether to cite AI, we will reference our use in the following way.
units.why: Example 1: 'we will be transparent in our use of AI in the completion of any classroom tasks' requires disclosure for all tasks; P24.

units.passage: It is your responsibility, however, to be transparent in that use.
units.why: 'It is your responsibility, however, to be transparent in that use' places disclosure on the student, P24.

units.passage: You are also required, for every assignment in this course, to submit an “AI Acknowledgement”. AI Acknowledgement: For every assignment submission, you will include a 150-300 word acknowledgment. Your acknowledgement should include, 1. The identification of the tool(s) you used, 2. An explanation of why you decided to use the tool(s), 3. A description of how you used the tool(s) to manage assignment requirements, and 4. A reflection on your experience using the tool, exploring what worked or didn’t, and acknowledging limitations of the tool for this assignment, potential biases, etc.
units.why: The sample says 'you are required, for every assignment in this course, to submit an "AI Acknowledgement"'. A disclosure submitted with every assignment is P24; the content of the acknowledgement is coded as its own unit (P26).

units.passage: When you do use generative-AI tools, you must be fully transparent with your use, including proper citation and any other documentation required by your instructor.
units.why: Example 4: 'you must be fully transparent with your use, including proper citation and any other documentation required by your instructor' requires disclosure and citation, P24.

units.passage: and to use any approved tools transparently and with proper acknowledgment, consistent with academic integrity standards.
units.why: Students are to 'use any approved tools transparently and with proper acknowledgment', a disclosure duty, P24.

units.passage: AI-generated content used in an official State capacity should include transparency of authorship. This includes citation for content that is AI generated or edited, and should disclose details of its review (how the material was reviewed, edited, by whom, and the date the system was used).
units.why: AI content used in a state capacity should show authorship transparency and citation, with details of review: disclosure (P24).

units.passage: Clearly note when AI is used especially in publicly facing works representing the university.
units.why: "Clearly note when AI is used especially in publicly facing works representing the university" is a disclosure rule, P24.

units.passage: Ideas and content generated by you, and those that are AI-generated, should be clearly delineated and cited accordingly.
units.why: The second sample says 'Ideas and content generated by you, and those that are AI-generated, should be clearly delineated and cited accordingly', a disclosure rule, P24.

units.passage: Transparency in students’ AI usage (i.e. being forthright about when and how AI tools were used in completing assignments or projects)
units.why: The integrity discussion lists '(1) Transparency in students' AI usage' (being forthright about when and how AI was used), a disclosure expectation, P24.

units.passage: Proper acknowledgment by students of AI assistance (similar to citing a source), when AI tools have contributed to idea generation, writing, problem -solving, or other academic tasks
units.why: '(2) Proper acknowledgment by students of AI assistance (similar to citing a source)' is an acknowledgment rule, P24.

units.passage: W&M should establish rules for appropriate GenAI use, including restrictions on inputting sensitive data and requirements to disclose GenAI-generated content
units.why: 'requirements to disclose GenAI-generated content' is the second usage rule W&M should establish, P24.

units.passage: You must clearly indicate in yo ur citations when and how you used AI for brainstorming purposes. It is an honor code offense to use AI tools for more than brainstorming without explicit permission. CATEGORY 4 - AI for Limited or Specific Tasks You may use AI tools as outlined by your instructor in the assignment guidelines.
units.why: 'You must clearly indicate in your citations when and how you used AI for brainstorming purposes' is disclosure with each submission (P24); student, during-work, must.

units.passage: You must clearly indicate in your citations when and how you used AI for these purposes
units.why: 'You must clearly indicate in your citations when and how you used AI for these purposes' (P24); student, during-work, must.

units.passage: Communicate when and how GenAI is used as appropriate for discipline and context.
units.why: 'Communicate when and how GenAI is used as appropriate for discipline and context' is a learning goal about disclosing AI use (P24); student, general, informs.

units.passage: Acknowledgement of AI Use: Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT 4o, Claude, and Copilot were used as thought partners and writing collaborators throughout the planning and writing of this document
units.why: 'Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT 4o, Claude, and Copilot were used as thought partners and writing collaborators' discloses AI use in writing the appendix, P24.

units.passage: How may students most effectively demonstrate that their work – whether in draft or final form – is either entirely their own or properly cited? (“You may incorporate AI-generated content or ideas in assignments, but you must cite this content, and you must fact-check all material, because AI-generated content often contains falsehoods and fictional sources. Citations must include which AI platform generated the content, and the specific prompts used to generate content
units.why: 'Citations must include which AI platform generated the content, and the specific prompts used' names the tool and the prompt, P25.

units.passage: Furthermore, you must cite Generative AI when it is used.
units.why: "you must cite Generative AI when it is used" is a disclosure duty with each submission, P24.

units.passage: All assignments that use any external source must be credited using a proper citation.
units.why: "All assignments that use any external source must be credited using a proper citation" requires crediting sources, P24 (with AI a covered source).

units.passage: Students are permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course if instructor permission is obtained in advance. Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools. Option 3: Use only with acknowledgement Students are permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course if that use is properly documented and credited.
units.why: Option 3 lets students use the tools "if that use is properly documented and credited", so AI use is conditional on attribution; P24 (disclose AI use with each submission).

units.passage: Develop a Practice of Transparency Faculty and students should cite their use of AI. When instructors thoughtfully acknowledge how AI has supported their work—in course design, writing, or research— they help students develop a more mature understanding of academic tools, agency, and intellectual ownership.
units.why: "Faculty and students should cite their use of AI" is a disclosure expectation for everyone: P24.

units.passage: At any level above UG 0, you must submit a written statement identifying any AI tools or AI-enabled features used and explaining how they were used in producing the work.
units.why: "you must submit a written statement identifying any AI tools or AI-enabled features used and explaining how they were used" requires disclosure with each submission (P24).

units.passage: Any AI use above UG 0 must be disclosed in writing.
units.why: "Any AI use above UG 0 must be disclosed in writing" is a disclosure requirement for submissions, P24.

units.passage: Because preparatory work is part of the assignment, this use must be disclosed.
units.why: "Because preparatory work is part of the assignment, this use must be disclosed" requires disclosure even of brainstorming (P24).

units.passage: A structured statement of work is ideal, but any written disclosure satisfies this requirement; what matters is that you put your AI use on the record and stand behind what you report.
units.why: "A structured statement of work is ideal, but any written disclosure satisfies this requirement" says what form disclosure may take, P24.

units.passage: Disclose the use of Generative AI tools: YU faculty and staff who leverage Generative AI to produce any written materials or other work product must disclose that those materials and that work product is based on or derives from the use of Generative AI. You must always be transparent if you are relying on the output of a Generative AI tool.
units.why: "YU faculty and staff who leverage Generative AI to produce any written materials or other work product must disclose" requires staff to disclose AI use (P24).
